# git runs `!` aliases from the worktree root, so with a nested sesam dir a
# plain `!sesam` alias looks for `.sesam/` at the root and fails. The alias has
# to return to the caller's directory first (git exports it as GIT_PREFIX) so
# `git sesam` behaves exactly like `sesam` run where the user is.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

mkdir vault
exec sesam init --user admin --sesam-dir vault
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# From inside the nested sesam dir the alias finds the repo like `sesam` does.
cd vault
exec git sesam ls
stdout 'README\.md'

# Relative paths resolve against the caller's cwd, not the worktree root.
mkdir sub
cp $WORK/secretfile sub/local
cd sub
exec git sesam add ./local --group admin
cd $WORK
grep 'sub/local' vault/sesam.yml

-- secretfile --
top secret
